hits.author: matyyyy
hits.story_text:
Hi HN!

I've been software engineer for about 15 years. For me this industry was always about learning. To be honest, I don't feel this anymore. I see more and more people delegating most of their work to LLMs. We rarely talk about software design or architecture, because Claude is such a great companion, so most of the workers don't need these technical discussions.

Sometimes I feel a bit lost. I am not sure, what should I learn to stay in the industry and to have opportunity to work on interesting problems.

I always saw HN as a place full of ambitious and creatives people. Inspired by hackertube.org and hackerbooks.org, I scanned HN comments in 2026 to extract learning materials recommended by community here, to help me decide with the next steps in my learning journey.

Best, Mateusz
hits.title: Show HN: What HN community recommended learning in 2026

hits.author: bcye
hits.story_text:
Hi HN!

I was missing a (travel) planning tool that would let me plan at any detail level and start with a rough sketch. I wanted the flexibility to just put post-its on parts that are not planned (in detail) and a more detailed plan for other parts.

So I built a map that you can mark up with drawings, markers and post-its. Additionally you can link to different boards from markers to i.e. plan a city within a larger trip.

It's built using Maplibre, with self-hosted Protomaps for the tiles and Yjs for state. Currently, state is saved locally in the browser with no login and you can ex- and import your boards as json files. In the future I will want to add some form of collaboration and sync though.

I'm very curious to hear how it fits your (travel and non-travel) use case and what features you still need.
hits.title: Show HN: Mapboard – Excalidraw, but on a Map
